newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY FREE DEMOCRATS SAY COALITION STILL VIABLE.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY FREE DEMOCRATS SAY COALITION STILL VIABLE.

text.p: Hungary's junior coalition partner Free Democrats (SZDSZ) said on Saturday their participation in the governing coalition with the Socialists has more advantages than drawbacks.

"It was worth entering this coalition because we could do a lot to make Hungary a more civilised, more prosperous country," party chairman Ivan Peto told a news conference following the SZDSZ annual convention.

After the 1994 general election, the Free Democrats formed a coalition government with the Socialist party -- which had won over 50 percent of the votes -- thus establishing a 72 percent majority in parliament.
However, Peto said there were and are misgivings within the party about the benefits of this political step.
"Those who were critical about entering the coalition, keep looking for arguments that sustain their view," Peto said.
One of the party's prominent figures, Istvan Eorsi, put forward a motion -- on which the convention decided not to vote -- wording criticism against Prime Minister Gyula Horn.
"The Prime Minister's governing style is contrary to the goals the government should pursue," Eorsi said in a draft motion.
According to a recent opinion poll, 62 percent of SZDSZ supporters say the party should stick to its governing role.
